question: Assume today is 2026-09-14. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of visitor arrivals to Hong Kong in September 2026, as it will be first reported (provisional figure) in the Hong Kong Tourism Board's monthly visitor arrivals press release.

target.what: Total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong from all source markets and travel modes, counted as person-trip arrivals of visitors (non-Hong Kong residents, including overnight and same-day visitors) during the calendar month, as the first provisional figure in the Hong Kong Tourism Board monthly visitor arr
target.cadence: Monthly press release; provisional first-release figure, later subject to revision
target.caveats: At the 2026-09-14 cutoff the target month is ongoing, so part of September 2026 is future and unobserved. methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed monthly total (p1) and applies a dimensionless September-to-July seasonal/trend factor. It is the most direct monthly run-rate route. Main failure modes: p1 revision, an abnormal September shock, or a seasonal factor outside the assumed range.

methods.rationale: Uses two overlapping HKTB cumulative totals to isolate June+July 2026 as a recent two-month run-rate, then applies a dimensionless September-to-that-period ratio. Sensitive to rounding/revision in p37 and to whether June-July is representative of September; the subtraction and factor are explicit.

p20.role: March 2026 total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong, all source markets and travel modes

a3.role: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to March 2026

methods.rationale: Uses March 2026, another shoulder-month total, as the level anchor and adjusts by a September-to-March factor. Shared dependence on HKTB totals and possible event-calendar differences are the main risks; the factor is deliberately near one but with a wide range.

p42.role: June 2024 provisional total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong

a4.role: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to June 2024, incorporating two-year growth and September-over-June seasonality

methods.rationale: Uses a credible older provisional monthly level (p42) but explicitly adjusts it for the 2024-to-2026 growth path and September seasonality. This provides an independent vintage anchor. Main risks: 2024 base abnormalities, revisions, and an unstable 2024-2026 growth path.

assumptions.name: Sep 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to Jul 2026
assumptions.rationale: July is a summer peak; September is usually somewhat lower in Hong Kong, though Mid-Autumn Festival on 25 Sep 2026 and pre-National Day traffic may support the month. July 2026 total growth had slowed to +2.6% with overnight arrivals down 3.9%, so a high extrapolation is not warranted. The range reflects typical shoulder-month softening versus July.
assumptions.applies_when: No major typhoon, border disruption or new travel-policy shock materially changes September from normal seasonal patterns after the 2026-09-14 cutoff.
assumptions.falsified_by: Credible HKTB historical data showing September consistently well above 0.99 of July, or evidence of a large September 2026 shock.

assumptions.name: Sep 2026 total relative to Jun+Jul 2026 combined total
assumptions.rationale: p2-p37 gives roughly 8.22m arrivals for June+July 2026; p1 implies July around 4.5m and hence June around 3.7m. September is one month versus two, and is likely near the June-July average, so about half the combined two-month total. The range allows September to be below July but above June.
assumptions.applies_when: The p37 first-five-months preliminary figure is not materially revised and June-July 2026 is a reasonable recent run-rate anchor.
assumptions.falsified_by: Large revision to p37 or evidence that September 2026 is far outside the June-July range.

assumptions.name: Sep 2026 total relative to Mar 2026
assumptions.rationale: March and September are both shoulder months. March 2026 recorded 4.35m with +14% year-on-year growth, but growth had moderated by July 2026 (+2.6% total), so September is assumed slightly below March rather than matching its growth momentum.
assumptions.applies_when: March 2026 event and holiday effects are broadly comparable in scale to September 2026 event/holiday effects.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 has a much stronger event calendar or that March 2026 was an unusual outlier.

assumptions.name: Sep 2026 total relative to Jun 2024 provisional
assumptions.rationale: June 2024 was 3.13m. The p2-p37-p1 bridge implies June 2026 around 3.7m, about 19% above June 2024; September is typically somewhat above June but below the July summer peak. Combining two-year growth and modest September-over-June seasonality gives roughly 1.30 times the June 2024 level.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2024-to-2026 growth path is broadly stable and September seasonality relative to June remains positive.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that June 2024 was abnormal, or that September 2026 is below June 2026 in Hong Kong.

a1.role: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to July 2026, dimensionless seasonal factor

methods.rationale: Round-1 route retained: latest available same-year run-rate p1 (July 2026) scaled by a September/July factor calibrated on p76/p78 (~0.78) and the 2023 analogue p61/p63/p82, nudged to 0.80 for July's weak YoY growth in p1. Covers all source markets and modes. Failure modes: a September-specific shock, a changed seasonal pattern, or July being an unrepresentative soft month.

p2.role: January-July 2026 cumulative total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong

p37.role: Preliminary first five months 2026 total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong, approximate, subtracted to isolate June+July 2026

a2.role: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to the June+July 2026 combined total, dimensionless

methods.rationale: Round-1 route retained: p2 minus p37 isolates a June+July 2026 block that internally agrees with p1; a2 applies the 2023-2024 September/(June+July) ratio from p76, p42, p78 and the 2023 analogue. Weaknesses: p37 is an approximate rounded statement, and the difference inherits revisions between the May and July releases; both are inside a2's range.

p76.role: September 2024 total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong

p92.role: 2025 annual total visitor arrivals year-on-year growth vs 2024, used as a proxy for the September 2024 to September 2025 growth step

a3.role: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to September 2025, dimensionless change factor

methods.rationale: Uses the only direct September level p76 (3.06M) and carries it to September 2025 with 2025 annual growth p92, then to September 2026 with a3. Support for the annual-growth proxy: p82 shows September 2024 itself grew 10.5%, close to the annual 2025 rate of 12% in p92. Main failure mode: September 2025 growth differed materially from the annual figure, which a3's range only partly absorbs.

p42.role: June 2024 provisional total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong

a4.role: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to June 2024, dimensionless factor combining seasonal and two-year growth

methods.rationale: p42 (June 2024, 3.13M) is a well-documented provisional level with nearly neutral September/June seasonality (p76 versus p42); a4 adds the 2024-2026 growth implied by p84/p92 and p2. It gives a cross-year anchor partly independent of the July 2026 anchor p1, though p42 and p76 come from the same HKTB measurement system.

assumptions.name: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to July 2026
assumptions.rationale: p76 September 2024 over p78 July 2024 gives ~0.78; the 2023 analogue from p61, p63 and p82 also gives ~0.77. September is post-summer and normally below July. I put the point at 0.80 because July 2026 growth was unusually weak in p1, which depresses this route's denominator. Range covers timing and typhoon effects.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows a normal post-summer pattern without a border, aviation or severe-weather shock, and p1 is a valid same-year pre-season anchor.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 arrivals are far above or below this fraction of July, e.g. a typhoon-driven closure, a new border policy, or a major event shifting September demand.

assumptions.name: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to June+July 2026 combined
assumptions.rationale: p76 September 2024 divided by p42 June 2024 plus p78 July 2024 gives ~0.43; the 2023 analogue from p76/p82, p61/p63 and p61 gives a similar ~0.44. The denominator built from p2 minus p37 inherits p37's approximate nature, which is inside the range.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2023-2024 seasonal ratio of September to the June+July block remains representative, and p37 is a usable approximation of first-five-month 2026 arrivals.
assumptions.falsified_by: September 2026 deviating far from the historical range relative to the June+July block, or evidence that p37 is materially misstated.

assumptions.name: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to September 2025
assumptions.rationale: 2026 growth decelerated from +17% in Q1 (p17) and +14% in March (p21) to +11.4% for Jan-Jul (p2) and +2.6% in July (p1). p84 with p92 shows 2025 annual arrivals about 12% above 2024. I therefore assume September 2026 is modestly above September 2025 rather than another double-digit year. This is a change factor, not a level of the target.
assumptions.applies_when: Recent deceleration continues and September 2026 YoY growth lands in the low-to-mid single digits.
assumptions.falsified_by: August/September 2026 data showing renewed double-digit growth or a year-on-year decline outside the stated range.

assumptions.name: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to June 2024 provisional
assumptions.rationale: p76 September 2024 is close to p42 June 2024, so September/June seasonality is near one. From June 2024 to September 2026, p84 with p92 gives ~12% for 2025 and p2 gives ~11.4% for Jan-Jul 2026, implying roughly a fifth of cumulative growth; the weak July 2026 growth in p1 argues against the top of the range. The factor combines near-neutral seasonality with two-year growth.
assumptions.applies_when: June 2024 is a valid seasonal base and the 2024-2026 growth path is not structurally broken.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large structural break in 2025-2026 arrivals, or a September/June seasonal ratio far from one.

methods.label: m1

p1.role: July 2026 total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong, all source markets and travel modes, person-trips

a1.role: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to July 2026, dimensionless seasonal factor

methods.rationale: Round-1 route retained: latest available same-year run-rate p1 (July 2026) scaled by a September/July factor calibrated on p76/p78 (~0.78) and the 2023 analogue p61/p63/p82, nudged to 0.80 for July's weak YoY growth in p1. Covers all source markets and modes. Failure modes: a September-specific shock, a changed seasonal pattern, or July being an unrepresentative soft month.

methods.label: m2

p2.role: January-July 2026 cumulative total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong

p37.role: Preliminary first five months 2026 total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong, approximate, subtracted to isolate June+July 2026

a2.role: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to the June+July 2026 combined total, dimensionless

methods.rationale: Round-1 route retained: p2 minus p37 isolates a June+July 2026 block that internally agrees with p1; a2 applies the 2023-2024 September/(June+July) ratio from p76, p42, p78 and the 2023 analogue. Weaknesses: p37 is an approximate rounded statement, and the difference inherits revisions between the May and July releases; both are inside a2's range.

methods.label: m3

p76.role: September 2024 total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong

p92.role: 2025 annual total visitor arrivals year-on-year growth vs 2024, used as a proxy for the September 2024 to September 2025 growth step

a3.role: September 2026 total visitor arrivals relative to September 2025, dimensionless change factor

methods.rationale: Uses the only direct September level p76 (3.06M) and carries it to September 2025 with 2025 annual growth p92, then to September 2026 with a3. Support for the annual-growth proxy: p82 shows September 2024 itself grew 10.5%, close to the annual 2025 rate of 12% in p92. Main failure mode: September 2025 growth differed materially from the annual figure, which a3's range only partly absorbs.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
